title: The Black coat on the hook
subtitle: 仪表穿着 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）
meta: 主题语境：仪表穿着（人与自我·生活与学习·个人仪表与穿着）　|　核心词汇：black　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 black 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1987 the director wrote of ① a black coat on the hook in the poster, and everybody in the theatre said at once that it was ② blacker than the one named there the year before. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the director, who never explained anything, had done it twice over and gone home; it was the black ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the blackest coat on the hook anybody in the theatre had ever seen, or so the poster for August 1981 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too black to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the actor who had come to help; the black ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the script at the far stage, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a black day for the family, and said that no actor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as black as the day for the family they had once had in the old theatre. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was black or not, and he said so.

By 1994 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the poster. What the line asked for was ⑦ something black, and nothing besides. The actor from the next theatre called the whole plan ⑧ quite black; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the poster kept the names of the black ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1997, year after year, she wrote of another black coat on the hook in the same poster, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ blacker than anybody had expected. ⑩ The blackest day for the family in the whole theatre, she said in 1999, was the one she could never quite name; the black ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 黑色（前置定语 a black coat on the hook：1987 年导演在戏报里记下的那件黑色的外套）
B. adj. 黑色／黯淡（比较级 blacker than：文中两处，一处比钩上的外套，一处比预想）
C. adj. 黑色／黯淡（最高级 the blackest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 黑色（表语 too black to do：母亲觉得它太黑色，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 黯淡（前置定语 a black day for the family：叔叔把整件事称作一桩黯淡的晦日）
F. adj. 黯淡（同级比较 as black as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩全家的晦日相比）
G. adj. 黯淡（后置定语 something black：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 黯淡（受程度副词修饰 quite black：那位演员的评价）

items.q: a black coat on the hook
the blackest coat on the hook anybody
a black day for the family
The blackest day for the family in

answers.why: black 意为“黑色”，1987 年导演在戏报里记下的是“一件黑色的外套”，此处作前置定语 a black coat on the hook。
black 意为“黑色”，此处用比较级 blacker than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
black 意为“黑色”，戏报上 八月 那行字说它是戏院里最黑色的一件，故用最高级 the blackest coat on the hook。
black 意为“黑色”，母亲认为这件东西“太黑色了，谁也用不上”，too black to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
black 意为“黯淡”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩黯淡的晦日”，此处作前置定语 a black day for the family。
black 意为“黯淡”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩全家的晦日一样黯淡”，同级比较用 as black as。
black 意为“黯淡”，戏报上那半行字要的是“黯淡的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something black。
black 意为“黯淡”，邻戏院来的那位演员认为这套计划“相当黯淡”，quite 修饰原级 black。
black 意为“黯淡”，1997 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要黯淡”，故用比较级 blacker than。
black 意为“黯淡”，母亲 1999 年说的是“整个戏院里最黯淡的那一桩”，故用最高级 the blackest day for the family。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1987 年，导演在戏报里记下了一件黑色的外套。（a black coat on the hook）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更黑色。（blacker than …）
母亲觉得它太黑色，谁也用不上。（too black to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩黯淡的晦日。（a black day for the family）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩全家的晦日一样黯淡。（as black as …）
到了 1994 年，戏报上只剩半行字：要的是一件黯淡的东西。（something black）
answers: In 1987 the director wrote of a black coat on the hook in the poster.
Everybody said it was blacker than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too black to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a black day for the family.
He said nobody would call it as black as the day for the family they had once had.
By 1994 the poster asked for nothing but something black.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 black 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1987 the director wrote of a black coat on the hook in the poster, and nobody forgot it.
It was the blackest coat on the hook in the theatre, or so the poster says.
My mother thought it too black to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a black day for the family, and nobody argued with him.
The actor from the next theatre called the plan quite black, and everybody laughed.
The black ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
